chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr al-Khazzāz, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the takbīr over funerals: is there in it anything fixed? He said: No. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم pronounced takbīr eleven, nine, seven, five, six, and four times.

As for what this report contains of increasing the takbīr beyond five times, it is abandoned by consensus. It is possible that he عليه السلام was reporting the act of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in that regard, because he would pronounce takbīr over one funeral or two, then another funeral would be brought, and he would begin from where he had ended, making five takbīrs; so when that is added to what he had already pronounced, it exceeds five takbīrs. That is permissible, as we have explained in our major book.

As for what it contains of four takbīrs, it is to be understood as a state of taqiyyah, because it is the doctrine of all those who opposed the Imāmiyyah; or it may be a report about the action of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم with the hypocrites or those suspected regarding Islam, for he عليه السلام used to act in that way. This indicates that.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under specific circumstances
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: the pronouncing of takbīr in the funeral prayer
key_terms.الْإِجْمَاعِ: scholarly consensus by which a ruling is upheld or a report’s apparent meaning is set aside
key_terms.الْجَنَائِزِ: funerals or funeral biers over which the prayer is performed
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقِينَ: hypocrites for whom a distinct prophetic practice is referenced
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: individual utterances of takbīr counted within the rite
key_terms.مُوَقَّتٌ: fixed or specifically determined in number

ai.seo_question: How are different numbers of takbīrs in funeral prayer understood in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report concerns the number of takbīrs in the funeral prayer and states that no single fixed number is indicated by the report itself in an unrestricted way. The accompanying explanation clarifies that anything above five takbīrs is not acted upon independently by consensus, and that reports mentioning four are interpreted through taqiyyah or specific cases such as funerals of hypocrites or those merely outwardly counted as Muslim.
